articles.title: investingLive Asia-Pacific market news: Chipmakers hit ahead of Nvidia
articles.description: AI: Daily quotas come to DeepSeek, a visible sign of China’s AI chip crunch BOJ’s Takata calls for nimble hikes after 1.5% bid, says neutral rate may top estimates Goldman sees Brent at $78 by end-2027 as oil surplus returns, flags near-term upside risk Records show $12bn Nvidia chips to China, US drafts licence rules on Nvidia chip exports Japan economy shrinks 0.1% in Q3, first fall in 4 quarters as inflation hits households China factory output slows to 4.8% in October, retail sales up just 0.4% as demand sags China’s October data shows the economy losing momentum on retail sales and industry output Morgan Stanley goes max overweight global stocks, sees 15% S&P 500 upside on AI capex Oil price analysis: Sellers are losing momentum, but $86.75 remains the danger line Weekend - Bitcoin fell to four-month low near $62,000 as crypto liquidations top $2 billion Gold slips toward $3,876 ahead of Warsh as Fed speakers line up behind tighter policy China house prices continue their downward spiral PBOC sets USD/ CNY reference rate for today at 6.7141 (vs. estimate at 6.7152) Goldman’s second gold forecast downgrade in a month turns its bear case into the base case ICYMI: Fed’s Jefferson says inflation is the key signal for rates, with PCE still at 3.6% Weekend: Bessent urges Nvidia to hire an outsider CEO, pouring cold water on a Huang comeback Japan Q3 GDP shrinks 0.1% annualised vs +0.3% expected as exports and consumers weigh US futures open firmer as Nasdaq leads, oil slips despite Iran tanker claims: 5 things ECB bond market intervention warning from Governor Knot. Can’t replace sound fiscal policy, Trump out of public view since Wednesday, fuelling speculation on his wherabouts Weekend - Blackstone’s QTS cuts AI data center debt sale 60% as investors push back on pricing ICYMI - Trump extends Jones Act waiver 90 days, foreign tankers moving oil in US Iran says supertanker with 2 million barrels sank after Hormuz mine strike, unconfirmed ECB’s Nagel says another rate hike ‘highly probable’ as energy prices push inflation New Zealand services PSI hits 3.5-year high at 51.7, fifth straight month of growth Weekend Fed speak: Collins backs steady, gradual rate hikes, cool on a bigger December move Sunday Fed talk: Schmid says inflation would still be near 3% without energy, Fed has work to do Jensen Huang weighs Nvidia comeback days after quitting over scandal, FT reports Nvida stock analysis before its earnings Gold futures rose Friday, but the rally failed. What I’m watching next week investingLive Americas market news wrap: Hawkish Fed worries ebb after PPI Summary: Japan’s economy shrank an annualised 0.1% in Q3, but BOJ hawk Takata argued for nimble hikes. The yen and JGBs barely moved. China’s industrial output, retail sales and investment all missed forecasts. Home prices fell for a 41st month. Korean chipmakers led regional losses, with SK Hynix down more than 6%, following weekend Nvidia and export-curb headlines. US futures gave up early gains ahead of Fed Chair Warsh’s speech at 17:00 GMT and Nvidia results on Tuesday. Brent held near $95 despite unconfirmed Iranian claims about a tanker sinking. Gold eased to around $3,873 and silver fell more than 3%. China confirmed a Xi-Trump-Putin summit in Shenzhen on November 19. Asian markets slipped on Monday as soft data from Japan and China met hawkish messages from central banks. Chipmakers led the losses as worries mounted over AI demand and US export curbs ahead of Nvidia’s results. Japan Japan’s economy contracted an annualised 0.1% in the third quarter, its first decline in four quarters and short of forecasts for 0.3% growth. Consumption fell as inflation squeezed households and net trade cut growth, though business investment rose a stronger-than-expected 1.6%. Economists said the miss is unlikely to derail Bank of Japan tightening. Board member Hajime Takata backed that view in a speech. He argued that 2026 marks a regime change calling for nimble, data-dependent rate hikes, and that Japan’s neutral rate may prove higher than markets expect. Markets largely shrugged off his remarks. USD/JPY was little changed around 159.65 and the 10-year JGB yield edged up to about 2.88%. The Nikkei fell about 1.6% to around 60,180 and the Topix lost roughly 0.7%. China China’s October activity data disappointed across the board. Industrial output grew 4.8%, below the 5.3% forecast. Retail sales rose just 0.4%, and fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% in the first ten months. New home prices fell for a 41st straight month, though the annual decline eased to its slowest in almost a year. Economists see little chance of fresh stimulus before year-end. The Shanghai Composite eased about 0.4%, while the Hang Seng bucked the trend, rising around 0.8%. Chips and AI Korean chipmakers took the brunt of the selling. SK Hynix sank more than 6% and Samsung Electronics fell about 4%, pulling the Kospi down roughly 2.6% and the Kosdaq more than 3%. The selling followed weekend headlines on Nvidia. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a “dramatic shakeup” at the company, and The Wall Street Journal reported that Washington is drafting rules to curb advanced chip exports to Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore. Separately, Chinese AI developer DeepSeek reportedly began rationing its free service, citing insufficient computing power. Morgan Stanley took the other side, moving to a maximum overweight on global equities on the view that the AI investment cycle remains intact. Nvidia reports on Tuesday. Fed and US US stock futures gave up early gains, with S&P 500 futures down about 0.2% and Nasdaq 100 futures off roughly 0.5%. Recent remarks from Fed officials Jeff Schmid, Susan Collins and Philip Jefferson all put inflation at the centre of policy, keeping a December rate hike firmly priced. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh opens a Fed conference on AI and productivity at 17:00 GMT (12:00 pm ET). Commodities and crypto Brent was steady near $95.40 and WTI was around $87.10. Expectations of a supply surplus offset unconfirmed Iranian claims that a supertanker sank after hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz. Goldman Sachs forecast Brent easing to $78 by end-2027, while flagging near-term upside risks from attacks on shipping. Gold eased to around $3,873 an ounce after Goldman cut its end-2027 forecast to $4,650, and silver fell more than 3%. Bitcoin hovered near $65,100 after hitting a four-month low around $62,000 over the weekend. Geopolitics China confirmed that President Xi Jinping will host the first trilateral summit with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on November 19, alongside the APEC gathering. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.
